prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1202; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- Witnesses and the officer say the claimant was not in the vehicle when the crash happened.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Insured reported a rear-end collision at a stop on a city street. The claimant, who is not represented by an attorney, says they were struck from behind and felt neck pain shortly afterward.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver of the insured vehicle is named on it. Coverage was in force at the time of loss, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant, who described the impact the same way as in the first report. They reported whiplash symptoms and said they have been seen at a clinic.

Entry 4: Received photos of the rear bumper and trunk of the claimant's vehicle. The damage is consistent with the impact described, and the photos show some of the scene details the claimant mentioned.

Entry 5: Obtained the police report. The officer and two bystanders who spoke at the scene state that the claimant was not inside the vehicle when the collision occurred, which conflicts with the claimant's account. No independent witness has been identified who can confirm the claimant's position.

Entry 6: Called the claimant to ask about the conflict in the accounts. They repeated the same description of the crash and said they had stepped out briefly before the collision, without changing any other detail.

Entry 7: Reviewed the medical records received so far. The whiplash diagnosis is plausible for a collision of this type, and no prior injury to the neck or upper back appears in the claimant's history. Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this injury.

Entry 8: Checked prior claims and vehicle history for the claimant's car. No earlier damage to the vehicle is on record, and nothing indicates an earlier injury claim involving the same body area.

Entry 9: Summarized the file for supervisor review. Medical treatment duration and the disputed position of the claimant at impact remain open items, and the damage and injury evidence are otherwise consistent with the reported loss. Next step is to request the treatment billing and a recorded statement from the claimant.
